In [9], this topology was shown to be capable of responding to CM insults using a simple control algorithm. However, the use of a sub-optimal control strategy results in a larger DC voltage transient and the need for an energy storage system to compensate. A better optimized control strategy will be developed here. The green encircled section of Fig. 1 shows the output stage of the full SST design in [9] which performs the switching necessary to address CM in- sults. The full converter is not considered in the scope of this paper because CM effects do not cross the DC links or the dual active bridge (DAB) cou- pling the input rectifier to the output inverter, as shown in [9]. The input rectifier and the output inverter may be treated independently as it relates to mitigation of CM current offset. In the proposed architecture, the fourth leg (far right leg) is shorted to neutral. Additionally, the DC bus is floating with respect to network ground. The output of the SST is coupled to the main grid. The CM insult voltage is modeled as a DC offset in the neutral path. Figure1: ProposedarchitectureofSSTforcommonmodemitigation.
